At age 36, more than two decades into his professional career, “Canelo” has still only been beaten by the sport’s best fighters. Terence Crawford, now retired, was the last to do so in 2025, following Dmitry Bivol three years earlier. Both defeated the Mexican star by decision. But this past weekend, “Canelo” showed he has more than enough left in his fistic arsenal to outclass the world’s best, even as he nears the end of his in-ring run. So, what’s next for boxing’s biggest star? A fight between “Canelo” and David Benavidez remains one of the biggest bouts the sport could book. It’s always seemed unrealistic, but now is a non-starter, considering trainer Eddy Reynoso’s comments that the matchup is now dead earlier this year . With Benavidez now being a unified cruiserweight world champion, there is too much of a gulf in weight between the division Benavidez is set to defend his WBA and WBO unified titles in (200 pounds), and the one “Canelo” fought in over the weekend (168 pounds). item.title: 49ers rookie Gracen Halton loses starting job but gains mentor in DeForest Buckner
item.description: Niners defensive tackle Gracen Halton stuffs Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane on a run attempt in the second half on Sept. 20 at Levi's Stadium. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle) Life has been pretty good lately for San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle Gracen Halton. The fourth-round rookie, who climbed San Francisco's depth chart to start the season amid a slew of injuries, filled in admirably for incumbent starters Alfred Collins and CJ West. He earned more playing time and met the moment in a Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks, etching his name into rivalry lore with a forced fumble and a recovery for a touchdown in a three-point win. During his first-ever NFL bye week, the good times continued to roll. Halton attended a team-wide Halloween party. Then he took a trip to his hometown San Diego before flying back to the Bay Area on Sunday. "Got down on the water and enjoyed my time," Halton told reporters Monday in Santa Clara. So, naturally, life had to take the 22-year-old down a peg. When the 49ers acquired defensive tackle DeForest Buckner in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts last week, Halton's starting role, which he had worked so hard to earn over the course of six months, vanished with the snap of a finger. Move over, rookie, and make way for a three-time Pro Bowler who also happens to be a fan favorite and one of the most recognizable figures of the Kyle Shanahan era. Upon learning that he was being supplanted, Halton surely felt disappointed. A slight bit of, what more could I have done? But the prevailing feeling, he said Monday inside the 49ers' locker room, was excitement. "I'm a young guy, so I've been watching (him) for a long time," Halton said with a smile. "I didn't realize how big he is in person. I was like, ‘This is a big dude!' "We're just glad that we got somebody that could help us. Another vet that's been here before. That knows what the culture is like. That knows what the standard is." Without knowing it, Buckner served as an early football role model for Halton. In the offseason leading up to his freshman season at Oklahoma, Halton said he watched Buckner, Dexter Lawrence II and a handful of other NFL defensive tackles work out at the Sooners' facility with private trainer Mark Hall. Halton remembered looking on with wide eyes and open ears, imagining the possibility of one day being Buckner's NFL peer. Four years later, they're teammates. "I was just a freshman watching those guys training at our facility," Halton said. "Now we on the same team in the league. It's crazy." Buckner is a natural leader. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he’s seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things.” RELATED: Experts release Oregon State vs. UTEP predictions, best bets, and preview for Week 4 Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won’t be able to focus all their offensive line on one side. “Teams have to respect his speed,” Hickle said. “If they don’t, then he’ll run right by them. item.title: INTERVIEW: Bayern boss Rouven Kasper takes swipe at Dortmund's 'Fan Mode' app as Carsten Cramer responds
item.description: INTERVIEW: Bayern boss Rouven Kasper takes swipe at Dortmund's 'Fan Mode' app as Carsten Cramer responds After Borussia Dortmund introduced a ‘Fan Mode’ feature in their club app to reward supporters staying off their phones during games, Bayern Munich's Chief Sales and Marketing officer, Rouven Kasper, said the Bavarians don't have the same issues in the stands. “I never heard about this [BVB app] because we don’t have this problem [at Bayern Munich]. We don’t need to tell anyone to take their phone away because our football is attractive," Kasper said at a media round in Munchen, attended by Bulinews.com. “This [Fan Mode app] is a marketing tool I have never had to think about. Maybe when you sit at home [watching a game the phone can be a problem], but I think in the Allianz Arena in Munich its not a problem. “For sure, mobiles are there [all the time] and for when we have influencers. But in the stadium, so far, there has never been an internal discussion that we need to think about a loyalty system [to reduce phone usage]. “However, I will discuss this [fan mode app] with a colleague later, we will see what the benefits are and then maybe we will think about it," the seemingly bewildered yet intrigued 44-year-old Bayern chief concluded. The following day, when informed about Kasper's opinions on the app, Borussia Dortmund CEO Carsten Cramer took time to defend the club's decision to put the loyalty scheme into operation. “I know this is a kind of marking activity [the Fan Zone app] but the marketing campaigns we develop should refer to the authenticity of the club," Cramer told Bulinews and other media present, referencing BVB's famous atmosphere. “The emotion of is our unique selling proposition. That is our most important currency. Of course, we want to make more money to invest in sport and infrastructure, but our most important currency is the love people give us. “The atmosphere at Signal Iduna Park is what makes Dortmund special. If you talk to the young players we signed in summer, one of their reasons for commitment was to play in front of this crowd. “They wanted to see these fans give their emotions to them. Sometimes it’s necessary to say we have some disadvantages [compared to Bayern], and others but we really have to fight for our place [in the market]. “We are still in the top 10 [of sales] in Europe. The competitors are the big sides in England, plus the two or three [clubs] in Spain, Italy and PSG. It makes us kind of proud what we have reached in the last decade," he summarized.

item.title: 3 Million Fans, 20 Stalkers, 24/7 Guards: Sophie Cunningham’s Fame Has a Dark Side
item.description: Aug 5, 2025; Los Angeles, California, USA; Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham arrives before the game against the LA Sparks at the Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Sophie Cunningham is a free agent guard who just saw her life change fast. This season, she has accumulated more new Instagram followers than the other 49 most-followed WNBA players combined, according to the New York Post . The numbers show she added over 2.9 million fans while playing for the Indiana Fever. A branding agency called bknown tracked the growth and shared the stats on Tuesday. Her account jumped from roughly 1.4 million to more than 4.3 million loyal followers. That is a huge win for the league, but it brings a dark side too. Just how powerful has Sophie Cunningham's social media influence been? She gained more Instagram followers this season than the other 49 most-followed WNBA players COMBINED… and more than ANY NBA player. pic.twitter.com/hJHsrwuEvb — Brendan Kaminsky (@BKaminsky) November 3, 2026 The fame she wanted has turned into a safety nightmare she never asked for. Cunningham said she cannot go anywhere without people recognizing her now. It used to be just certain spots, but now it is everywhere she goes. She told a podcast host that she hired security to travel with her 24/7 . They will start working for her next week to keep her safe from the crowds. This move comes after she admitted to having serious trouble with people watching her every move. The Stalkers Are Real Cunningham told Theo Von on his podcast that she has twenty stalkers the FBI is watching. She said there are a lot of crazy people out there who mean harm. One man named Kevin Singh even sent her a package containing a Guns N’ Roses shirt. He was arrested on felony charges in June and is locked away now. The 48-year-old delivered the letter and shirt to the Fever arena back in September 2025. It is a scary reality for a player who just wanted to speak her mind. Her comments on transgender athletes in sports sparked the war that brought this heat. She told ESPN in July that she wants to protect young girls from biological men. Those words made her a lightning rod for fans who agree and groups who rally against her. The backlash has been so intense that her daily routine has been stopped cold. She cannot just walk down the street or grab coffee like a normal person anymore. The cost of her voice is high, and the price is her privacy. Keeping It Real Despite the fear, Cunningham says she does not pay attention to her mean critics. She told her co-host Drew Hanlen that she is still a dweeb at heart. She believes the people who hate her are unhappy or just psychotic with hatred. She says she can handle it if they want to take it out on her. That attitude is strong, but hiring twenty-four-seven guards shows the danger is real. You do not bring in security unless the threat is very serious. Recently, the Indiana Fever suffered a first-round playoff defeat against the Aces.

item.title: Carrick: “Roma are a great team, it was always going to be difficult.”
item.description: Carrick: “Roma are a great team, it was always going to be difficult.” Following United’s 3-2 comeback win, Red Devils manager Michael Carrick spoke at a press conference analyzing the match against Roma. “I’m really proud of my players; they deserve great respect for being able to turn the game around. The fans also did their part; they wanted to inspire us, and their support was palpable.” “After the first half, there was a lot of frustration, but in the locker room, I reminded the boys how important the fans were. In the second half, we maintained a positive attitude and continued to believe until the end. It’s still a victory, nothing more.” “It’s certainly a very significant result. Some players experienced sensations they hadn’t yet experienced at Old Trafford, and for the new arrivals, it was crucial to feel the support of the fans. Sometimes, it’s not easy to figure out how to overcome difficulties. Now, however, we must stay calm and focus on the next match.” “We weren’t in an easy situation. Roma are a top-notch team, they marked the entire pitch individually, and we knew it would be a tough match. We left our opponents too much space, but gradually we managed to get closer to their goal. We knew they could cause us problems, but in those moments you have to keep believing in what you’re doing, without giving in to frustration.” “In the first half, we could have lost confidence, especially after what happened to Bruno Fernandes on the penalty and Baleba’s exit. Tielemans made a good impact coming off the bench. We wanted to give this victory to our fans.”

item.title: Football world mourns Tenerife striker De Miguel
item.description: Tributes were paid at matches across Europe on Tuesday night [Getty Images] The world of football has come together to mourn the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel . The forward suffered head and chest injuries in a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Spanish second division match against FC Andorra on Monday. De Miguel's condition was described as stable but serious on Monday, but his health deteriorated on Tuesday morning and the Spaniard died at 07:00 GMT. A minute's silence was held before Tuesday evening's Champions League matches across Europe. That will be repeated for Wednesday's fixtures, as well as all Europa League and Conference League matches this week. Mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez, Tenerife's home ground. Tenerife said in a statement on Tuesday evening they will commence six official days of mourning, with all club activities suspended during this time. The club's players, staff and officials will attend De Miguel's funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, Toledo. Tenerife will also open their home ground on Saturday evening to allow supporters to "bid a fitting farewell". "Jesus de Miguel's family would like to thank everyone for their messages of support and, from the bottom of their hearts, ask that their privacy be respected at this terrible time. May he rest in peace," added the statement. Jesus de Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 on a three-year deal [Getty Images] "We are torn by the news," said Fran Leon, president of Tenerife's federation of supporters' clubs. "All of the island is in mourning. All of Canarias is in mourning. It's a shared pain." Fan David Tejera said De Miguel's "effort" and "passion" for Tenerife would endure. "You are already part of the blue and white history," he said. Tenerife and Andorra were tied 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred. Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel. The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's ground to hospital. Players from both teams were visibly distressed by the incident, with a number of De Miguel's team-mates in tears. Before Spanish club Villareal's fixture against Paris St-Germain, fans held up a sign that read 'DEP' - which translates to descanse en paz, or rest in peace in English [Getty Images] 'Very difficult moment' for Owono Reuters reported on Tuesday that police in Spain have opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel's death. Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry. Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui told Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings were "very unlikely". The referee showed Owono a straight red card before abandoning the match

They don't offer much, whether because of their recent play, matchups, or other key factors. You will have to trust me on this and roll with someone else for an impending victory. item.title: Eckert explains star man’s absence in Southampton’s draw with West Brom
item.description: Eckert explains star man’s absence in Southampton’s draw with West Brom Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert is optimistic Leo Scienza will return for Saturday’s game against Preston after the winger missed his side’s 1-1 draw against West Brom through injury. Scienza was absent from the Saints squad after struggling with “pain”, Eckert said, having played through the problem in his previous appearance. Eckert revealed the Brazilian had been unable to feature against West Brom but is hopeful he will recover in time for Southampton’s weekend clash. “Yeah, he has pain,” Eckert explained. “It’s just so much pain, and he pushed through in the last game as well, but I’m very positive that he’ll be back for Saturday.” Reflecting on the draw, in which Samuel Edozie equalised for the Saints in the second half, Eckert said: “We changed that at half-time. I think the second half was a completely different game. There were a couple of chances in there to win it in the second half. “But I think if you look at the 90 minutes today, you take the point. I think it’s a fair result. We will take the point and move on to Preston.”

item.title: ‘Neither side of the aisle likes Stephen A. Smith’: Poll shows bad news for ESPN star
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Stephen A. Smith has spent the past couple of years teasing a potential run for president. While he has has repeatedly said he isn’t interested, but he also hasn’t completely closed the door. Now a new poll offers a mixed picture of what his political future could look like, as a small but real slice of voters would back him, but plenty more are quite actively against him. The good news The Bulwark and Pablo Torre Finds Out teamed up with YouGov to survey 1,417 American adults from Oct. 10-14 about politics and sports. Smith was among the figures included. As Awful Announcing noted, the poll found that at least 6 percent of respondents would vote for Smith as an independent candidate in hypothetical 2028 matchups. That held whether the Democratic nominee was Gavin Newsom, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Mark Cuban, or Pete Buttigieg, with JD Vance as the Republican nominee. Smith also drew 6 and 7 percent support in separate vice presidential questions on tickets led by Cuban and Arizona Sen. Mark Kelly. That’s a notable jump from a January 2025 poll, when just 2 percent of respondents said they would vote for him. The bad news While those numbers might seem to paint an optimistic outlook on Smith’s potential political career, the rest of the numbers weren’t anywhere near as kind. “By contrast, neither side of the aisle likes Stephen A. Smith,” Brendan Hartnett of The Bulwark wrote. “His net favorability is 10 points underwater with Harris voters and 3 points underwater with those who voted for Trump.” Among Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents, Smith didn’t fare much better as a potential running mate. “Thirty percent say Stephen A. Smith would be an unacceptable nominee, compared to only 7 percent who would be excited to have him on the ticket,” Hartnett wrote. Men were also twice as likely as women to have an opinion of Smith, 67 percent compared to 34 percent. According to Hartnett, “those opinions skew negative.” Smith’s background could be a problem, too. Just 5 percent of respondents said they would be more likely to vote for a candidate who was a TV commentator, while 43 percent said they’d be less likely. Smith has said that the biggest thing holding him back from a run is giving up his nine-figure salary at ESPN. Based on these numbers, he might want to hold onto it for now. item.title: History made. Liberty High player commits to Nebraska for flag football
item.description: Makenna Johnson is officially part of Arizona high school history. Johnson, a senior flag football player for Peoria Liberty, committed to Nebraska on Nov. 2, becoming the first active Arizona prep flag player to commit to a Power Four school for varsity flag football. Nebraska is the only current Power Four school that offers flag football as a varsity sport, which is in the NCAA Emerging Sports program. “It’s super exciting that I get to pave this path for young girls who are just joining flag football or who have been playing for a while now,” Johnson told The Arizona Republic. “It’s amazing. I’m blessed to be in this position.” Johnson is a two-way player at wide receiver and defensive back. She was on The Republic’s preseason top 10 list for both wide receiver and defensive back . Through 10 games this season, Johnson has 83 receptions for 935 yards and 12 touchdowns on offense and has recorded four interceptions so far. Liberty is 8-6 so far and is gaining steam as one of the favorites to make the 6A state championship game. At Nebraska, coaches Liz and Katie Sowers operate a system where players specialize on one side of the ball. It’s too early to tell if Johnson will play offense or defense at Nebraska, but she likes both sides. Johnson recently visited the school on her official visit this past weekend, from Oct. 30 to Nov. 1. It was a tough decision for Johnson, who has been playing basketball for a long time and was focused on that sport for most of her high school career. The 2025-26 school year was the first season of flag football at Liberty, which became a sanctioned Arizona Interscholastic Association sport in 2023. “Me and my family had a lot of good conversations, I prayed about it a ton,” Johnson said. “Once we got to Nebraska, I knew that was the place I had to be. All the opportunities there. The opportunity in general would be really hard to pass up. The coaches and players I encountered, I knew the people would make the place.” Liberty coach Josh Ahlvin has watched Johnson quickly emerge as a top player. Johnson was on the club team at Liberty before it became a varsity sport. Ahlvin had to work to convince Johnson that she had a future in flag football. “We talked four years ago when she was a freshman and we started the spring program the first year, those conversations we had back then kind of (fell) on deaf ears, jokingly. Her being able to go on a full ride to the University of Nebraska is remarkable.” Johnson will be the second flag football player from Arizona to join Nebraska. Tucson Salpointe Catholic alum Rylen Bourguet joined the team in 2026, transferring from Arizona State University. The two got to meet on Johnson’s visit. “I’ve heard a lot about her,” Johnson said. “It’s cool knowing someone from Arizona, having that connection there.” A third Arizona prep could join Nebraska, as Gilbert Highland junior quarterback Lacie Nemchick also has an offer from the Cornhuskers.
